mainTopic: Preparing מנחות, how many loaves each מנחה is baked into (ten or twelve) and why, and שמואל's ruling on four תודה loaves
overview: The משנה teaches that the wheat for every מנחה needs 300 rubbings and 500 strikings. The תנא קמא says this is done to the kernels, and רבי יוסי says it is done to the dough. רבי יהודה and רבי מאיר then argue whether most מנחות are baked as ten loaves or as twelve. The גמרא explains the pattern of rubbing and striking. It leaves רבי ירמיה's counting question as תיקו, and it brings a ברייתא to clarify רבי יוסי. Next it gives sources for the numbers. Twelve for לחם הפנים is written in the פסוק, and twelve for חביתי כהן גדול comes from a גזרה שוה. רבי יהודה learns ten for other מנחות from לחמי תודה, after weighing them against לחם הפנים and the חביתין. רבי מאיר's twelve comes from the חביתין or from לחם הפנים, depending on whether a rule learned by a גזרה שוה can teach through a בנין אב. Finally, שמואל rules that four big תודה loaves are enough after the fact. The גמרא defends this against several challenges, and its answer to a ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: משנה: 300 rubbings and 500 strikings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that every מנחה needs 300 rubbings and 500 strikings. The תנא קמא says these are done to the wheat, and רבי יוסי says they are done to the dough.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All מנחות need 300 rubbings and 500 strikings. The rubbing and striking are done to the wheat kernels. רבי יוסי says: they are done to the dough.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a rule about preparing the flour for every מנחה: it must be rubbed 300 times and struck 500 times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees about the numbers, 300 and 500. They argue about when this is done. The first opinion says it is done to the wheat kernels before grinding, and רבי יוסי says it is done to the dough after the flour is mixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offerings, sacrifices made from flour
Rubbing (with the hand)
Striking or pounding (with the fist or palm)
Wheat kernels
Dough

phrases.english: MISHNA: All the meal offerings require
three hundred rubbings
and five hundred strikings;
the rubbing and striking are done on the wheat kernels.
And Rabbi Yosei says: on the dough.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמְּנָחוֹת טְעוּנוֹת שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת שִׁיפָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every מנחה requires 300 rubbings and 500 strikings. The תנא קמא places this on the wheat, and רבי יוסי places it on the dough.

steps.title: משנה: ten loaves or twelve loaves
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says most מנחות are baked as ten loaves, except לחם הפנים and חביתי כהן גדול, which are twelve. רבי מאיר says most are twelve, except the loaves of תודה and נזירות, which are ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: All מנחות come as ten loaves each, except לחם הפנים and חביתי כהן גדול, which come as twelve. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי מאיר says: they all come as twelve, except the loaves of תודה and of נזירות, which come as ten each.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second argument: how many loaves or wafers a מנחה is baked into.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's basic rule is ten, with two exceptions that are twelve. רבי מאיר flips it: his basic rule is twelve, with the תודה and נזיר loaves as the exceptions that are ten.

keyTerms.meaning: The showbread placed on the שֻׁלְחָן in the מִקְדָּשׁ
The daily griddle-cake offering of the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
The loaves that come with a thanks offering
Naziriteship; here, the loaves brought when a נָזִיר finishes his term
Ten each, ten from each portion

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two opinions. Each one has a basic rule and exceptions, and they are opposites: רבי יהודה's basic rule is ten, and רבי מאיר's basic rule is twelve.

phrases.english: All the meal offerings come as ten loaves each,
phrases.notes: Ten loaves from each עִשָּׂרוֹן, the tenth-of-an-איפה measure of flour.

phrases.english: except for the showbread
and the griddle-cakes of the High Priest,
which come as twelve;
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּם בָּאוֹת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: They all come as twelve,
except for the loaves of the thanks offering and of naziriteship,
which come as ten each.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: ten is the rule, and לחם הפנים and חביתין are twelve. רבי מאיר: twelve is the rule, and תודה and נזיר loaves are ten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה says most מנחות are ten loaves, except לחם הפנים and חביתין, which are twelve. רבי מאיר says most are twelve, except תודה and נזירות loaves, which are ten.

steps.title: The order of rubbing and striking
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains the pattern: rub once and strike twice, then rub twice and strike three times.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught: He rubs once and strikes twice. He rubs twice and strikes three times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains how to actually perform the 300 rubbings and 500 strikings from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One round of the pattern is 3 rubbings and 5 strikings. Doing the round 100 times gives exactly the 300 and 500 the משנה requires.

keyTerms.meaning: He rubs
He strikes

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught: He rubs once,
strikes twice.
He rubs twice, strikes three times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to carry out the numbers in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rubbing and striking are done in rounds of rub-1, strike-2, rub-2, strike-3.

steps.title: Does back-and-forth count as one rubbing or two?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether moving the hand forward and back counts as one rubbing or as two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: Is moving the hand forward and bringing it back one rubbing, or perhaps is forward and back two? What is the answer?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks how to count the rubbings: does a full forward-and-back motion count once or twice?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This affects how much work the 300 rubbings take. If each direction counts, 150 back-and-forth motions are enough. If a full motion counts only once, you need 300 full motions.

keyTerms.meaning: Moving it forward, taking it away
Bringing it back
Or perhaps, the second side of a question
One / two

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
Is moving forward and bringing back one rubbing,
or perhaps moving forward and bringing back is two?
What is the answer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to count one unit of the rubbing described in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a back-and-forth hand motion counts as one שיפה or two

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: רבי ירמיה's question is left without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer to רבי ירמיה's question, so the question stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no source decides the matter either way. Both possibilities about how to count the rubbings remain open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 4 without an answer
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether back-and-forth counts as one rubbing or two is left undecided.

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי mean only dough, or also dough?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks whether רבי יוסי means the rubbing is done instead of on the wheat, or in addition to the wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: Rubbing and striking are done on the wheat; רבי יוסי says: on the dough. A question was asked: on the dough and not on the wheat? Or perhaps also on the dough?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the argument in the משנה and asks what exactly רבי יוסי means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's short word 'בבצק' can be read two ways. Either he replaces the wheat with the dough, or he adds the dough on top of the wheat, so the process is done twice.

keyTerms.meaning: And not, meaning instead of
Also, meaning in addition to

phrases.english: The משנה said: Rubbing and striking are done on the wheat;
Rabbi Yosei says: on the dough.
A question was asked before them:
Does he mean on the dough and not on the wheat,
or perhaps also on the dough?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the counting question and returns to the argument in step 1
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוסי puts the rubbing on the dough instead of the wheat, or in addition to it

steps.title: A ברייתא answers the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יוסי says plainly 'rubbing and striking on the dough', set against the first opinion's 'on the wheat'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught: Rubbing and striking are done on the wheat. רבי יוסי says: Rubbing and striking are done on the dough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question of step 6 from a ברייתא that spells out רבי יוסי's view more fully.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יוסי repeats the whole phrase 'שיפה ובעיטה' and puts it on the dough, directly opposite the wheat. This suggests he moves the process to the dough instead of adding a second round.

keyTerms.meaning: Rubbing and striking on the dough, רבי יוסי's full wording in the ברייתא

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught:
Rubbing and striking are done on the wheat;

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שִׁיפָה וּבְעִיטָה בַּבָּצֵק.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: Rubbing and striking are done on the dough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא presents רבי יוסי as placing the whole rubbing-and-striking process on the dough, opposite the wheat. This points to 'on the dough and not on the wheat'.

steps.title: Twelve loaves of לחם הפנים are written in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins finding sources for רבי יהודה's twelve-loaf exceptions. For לחם הפנים, the number twelve is written in the פסוק itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: All מנחות come, etc. Twelve for לחם הפנים: it is written explicitly about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second part of the משנה and starts explaining where the number twelve comes from, beginning with the easy case of לחם הפנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For לחם הפנים no derivation is needed, because the תורה itself says to bake twelve loaves. This sets up the harder question still to come: where do we learn twelve for חביתי כהן גדול?

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly, openly
It is written (in the פסוק)
Et cetera; the rest of the quote from the משנה

phrases.english: The משנה said: All the meal offerings come, etc.
The twelve loaves of the showbread:
it is written explicitly about it.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:5

steps.whyThisMatters: By saying לחם הפנים is the obvious case, the גמרא signals that the real work is still ahead: finding a source for twelve in the חביתין.
steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים בְּהֶדְיָא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section on the second argument of the משנה (step 2)
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Twelve loaves of לחם הפנים are stated explicitly in the תורה.

steps.title: חביתי כהן גדול get twelve through a word link
steps.stepSummary: The twelve loaves of חביתי כהן גדול are learned from לחם הפנים, because the word חֻקָּה appears in both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: The griddle-cakes of the כהן גדול come as twelve because the word 'obligation' (חֻקָּה) is written by them and also by לחם הפנים, which has twelve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps going through רבי יהודה's twelve-loaf exceptions. Now it gives the source for the second one, the כהן גדול's daily griddle-cake offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לחם הפנים had twelve written right in the פסוק. The חביתין do not, so the גמרא links them to לחם הפנים with a גזרה שוה built on the shared word חֻקָּה. That link brings the number twelve over to the חביתין.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily griddle-cake meal offering of the High Priest
'It comes': it is learned from (usually through a word link)
'Obligation' or 'statute': the shared word that links the two offerings
The showbread: twelve loaves placed on the שולחן in the מקדש

phrases.english: The griddle-cakes of the High Priest:
it is learned from 'obligation' and 'obligation'
phrases.notes: The word חֻקָּה appears in ויקרא 6:15 (the griddle-cakes) and ויקרא 24:9 (the showbread).

phrases.english: from the showbread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources for רבי יהודה's twelve-loaf exceptions, moving from לחם הפנים to חביתי כהן גדול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חביתי כהן גדול come as twelve, learned from לחם הפנים through the גזרה שוה of חֻקָּה–חֻקָּה.

steps.title: Why do all other מנחות come as ten?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי יהודה's rule that every regular מנחה is baked as ten loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the other meal offerings come as ten loaves each. Where do we learn that from?
steps.whatsHappening: After finishing the twelve-loaf exceptions, the גמרא turns to the general rule and asks where 'ten' comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exceptions (twelve) each have a source. The basic rule of ten for most מנחות still needs one too. This question sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offerings (flour offerings)
'From where do we know?': a request for a source

phrases.english: All the meal offerings
that come as ten each,
from where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַמְּנָחוֹת דְּבָאוֹת עֶשֶׂר עֶשֶׂר, מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the twelve-loaf exceptions to the general ten-loaf rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי יהודה's rule that all regular מנחות come as ten loaves.

steps.title: Ten is learned from לחמי תודה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from לחמי תודה, which come in groups of ten, that all other מנחות are ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from the loaves of the קרבן תודה. Just as there each kind is ten, so here too it is ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the number ten is borrowed from the loaves that come with a קרבן תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תודה loaves come in sets of ten of each type. רבי יהודה compares the regular מנחות to them with a simple 'just as there, so too here' comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: The loaves brought along with a thanks offering, in sets of ten
He learns it (derives it) from
'Just as there, so too here': the form of a comparison

phrases.english: He learns it from the loaves of the thanks offering:
just as there it is ten,
so too here it is ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten-loaf rule is learned by comparison to לחמי תודה, which come as ten.

steps.title: Why not learn twelve from לחם הפנים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: maybe the regular מנחות should be compared to לחם הפנים instead, and need twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why not learn from לחם הפנים? Just as there it is twelve, here too it should be twelve!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. There is another offering of loaves to compare to, and it has twelve, not ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both לחמי תודה and לחם הפנים are possible models. Choosing one over the other changes the number, so the גמרא wants a reason for choosing the תודה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But let him learn': opens a challenge proposing a different source

phrases.english: But let him learn it from the showbread:
just as there it is twelve,
so too here it should be twelve!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the choice of source in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of לחמי תודה as the model for regular מנחות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לחם הפנים is an equally possible model, and it would give twelve, not ten.

steps.title: Regular מנחות look more like לחמי תודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lists six ways regular מנחות are like לחמי תודה and unlike לחם הפנים, so the תודה is the better model.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes more sense to learn from לחמי תודה, since they share these features: brought by one person, brought as a donation, made with oil, become invalid overnight, not brought on שבת, and not brought in טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that regular מנחות have more in common with the תודה loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the list is a feature shared by regular מנחות and לחמי תודה but not by לחם הפנים. לחם הפנים is a public, required offering with no oil. It stays on the שולחן for days, is set up on שבת, and is brought even in טומאה. More similarity means the better comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It stands to reason': it makes more sense
An individual (as opposed to the public)
One who volunteers: a donated, not required, offering
Becomes disqualified (here, by being left overnight)
Ritual impurity

steps.confusionAlert: The six words are not separate rules. Each one is a short tag for a way the regular מנחות match the תודה loaves and differ from לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: It stands to reason that from the thanks-offering loaves
he should learn,
since they share: an individual, one who donates,
oil, becoming disqualified,
phrases.notes: נִפְסָל means invalid if left overnight; לחם הפנים stays on the שולחן for days.

phrases.english: not on Shabbat, and not in impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִלַּחְמֵי תוֹדָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Greater similarity: the model with more shared features wins.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לחם הפנים is just as good a model, so the number should be twelve.
steps.terutzMaskana: Regular מנחות share six features with לחמי תודה, so ten is correct.

steps.title: On the contrary: the מנחות look like לחם הפנים too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back with four features regular מנחות share with לחם הפנים and not with לחמי תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! He should learn from לחם הפנים, since they share: most-holy status, frankincense, being only מצה, and being brought by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the argument around and lists ways regular מנחות are actually closer to לחם הפנים. This reopens the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular מנחות and לחם הפנים are קדשי קדשים, have לבונה, are only מצה, and stand on their own. The תודה loaves are lesser holiness, have no לבונה, include חמץ, and come along with an animal קרבן. Now both sides have a list, and the next step weighs them against each other.

keyTerms.meaning: 'On the contrary': turns the argument the other way
Holy status (here: of the most holy level)
Frankincense
'Itself': brought on its own, not alongside an animal offering

phrases.english: On the contrary,
from the showbread he should learn,
since they share: consecrated status, and frankincense,
phrases.notes: He means the most-holy level; the תודה loaves are a lower level of holiness.

phrases.english: unleavened bread, and being by itself!
phrases.notes: וָעֶצֶם means brought on its own, while the תודה loaves come along with an animal קרבן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, מִלֶּחֶם הַפָּנִים הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the answer of step 13 with a list of opposing similarities.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 13 that regular מנחות are more like לחמי תודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Regular מנחות also share four features with לחם הפנים, so the similarity argument cuts both ways.

steps.title: The six likenesses outweigh the four
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 14. The six ways regular מנחות are like לחמי תודה are more than the four ways they are like לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the pushback from step 14 in two words: the list that points to לחמי תודה is longer, so it wins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 gave six likenesses to לחמי תודה, and step 14 gave four likenesses to לחם הפנים. Since both sides have points, the גמרא settles it by counting. Six beats four, so regular מנחות follow לחמי תודה and come as ten.

keyTerms.meaning: They are more numerous (there are more of them)
These (here, the six likenesses listed in step 13)

phrases.english: These are more numerous.
phrases.notes: "These" means the six likenesses to לחמי תודה from step 13, against only four for לחם הפנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the step 14 pushback by weighing the two lists of likenesses against each other.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing: the side with more shared features is the better model
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since regular מנחות share four features with לחם הפנים, maybe they should come as twelve.
steps.terutzMaskana: The six shared features with לחמי תודה outnumber the four, so regular מנחות follow לחמי תודה and come as ten.

steps.title: Why not learn twelve from חביתי כהן גדול?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a new model. The חביתי כהן גדול come as twelve, so maybe regular מנחות should learn from them and also be twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we hold that something learned through a גזירה שוה can then go on to teach through a בנין אב, let us learn from the חביתי כהן גדול: just as there it is twelve, so too here it should be twelve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge. Maybe regular מנחות should copy the חביתי כהן גדול, which come as twelve loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חביתין themselves only get their number twelve through a גזירה שוה from לחם הפנים. So using them as a model for other מנחות works only if a rule learned by a גזירה שוה can be passed on again through a בנין אב. If it can, the חביתין are a new rival to לחמי תודה, and they point to twelve, not ten.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule learned by matching a shared word in two פסוקים
Using one case as a model to set the rule for similar cases
A rule that was itself learned can turn around and teach another case
The griddle-cake מנחה the כהן גדול brings every day

steps.confusionAlert: The twelve of the חביתין is not written directly in the תורה. It comes from a גזירה שוה with לחם הפנים. That is why the גמרא opens with "if we hold": the whole challenge depends on whether a rule learned this way may be passed on again.

phrases.english: And if we hold
that a matter learned through a גזירה שוה
can turn around and teach through a בנין אב,
let us learn from the griddle-cakes of the כהן גדול:
just as there, it is twelve,
phrases.notes: "There" means the חביתין, which come as twelve loaves.

phrases.english: so too here, it should be twelve?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סְבִירָא לַן דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּבִנְיַן אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After לחם הפנים was set aside, the גמרא brings a different twelve-loaf model to challenge the derivation from לחמי תודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's derivation of ten loaves from לחמי תודה (step 11)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a rule learned through a גזירה שוה can teach again, the חביתין are an available model, and they would make regular מנחות twelve instead of ten.

steps.title: לחמי תודה are still the better model
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that it makes more sense to learn from לחמי תודה. Regular מנחות share six features with them that the חביתין lack.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands to reason that he should learn from לחמי תודה, since they are brought by a regular person, they are donated, they are not brought in halves, they can become פיגול, they are not brought on שבת, and they are not brought in טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the חביתין as a model. It lists six short points that show regular מנחות are much closer to לחמי תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the list is a way regular מנחות and לחמי תודה match, while the חביתין are different. The חביתין are brought by the כהן גדול, not a regular person. They are required, not donated. They are split into halves, morning and afternoon. They are never eaten, so they cannot become פיגול. They are brought even on שבת and even in טומאה. With six differences, the חביתין are a poor model, so the number stays ten.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it stands to reason
A regular person (not the כהן גדול)
Halves (the חביתין are offered half in the morning, half in the afternoon)
An offering ruined by the plan to eat it past its proper time
Ritual impurity

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה's ten loaves for regular מנחות come from לחמי תודה. Both twelve-loaf models, לחם הפנים and חביתי כהן גדול, are rejected because regular מנחות share more features with לחמי תודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא picks a model when a case looks like several sources: it lines up the shared features and follows the closest match.

phrases.english: It stands to reason that from the loaves of the תודה
he should learn,
since they are brought by a regular person,
by one who donates, and not in halves;
phrases.notes: The חביתין are required, not donated, and are offered half in the morning and half in the afternoon.

phrases.english: they can become פיגול, they are not brought on שבת,
and they are not brought in impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִלַּחְמֵי תוֹדָה הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the step 16 challenge by showing that the חביתין are a weaker match than לחמי תודה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparing features: the closer model wins
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חביתין, which come as twelve, could serve as the model for regular מנחות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Regular מנחות share six features with לחמי תודה that the חביתין lack, so they follow לחמי תודה and come as ten.

steps.title: חביתי כהן גדול share even more features
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues the opposite. Regular מנחות share eight features with חביתי כהן גדול that לחמי תודה do not have, so the חביתין should be the model.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! He should have learned from חביתי כהן גדול. Like regular מנחות, they are one tenth of an איפה. They become holy in a service vessel. They are fully consecrated. They come with לבונה. They are all מצה. They are brought on their own. They are brought near the מזבח. They are placed on the מזבח fires. And these features are more in number.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 17. It lists features that regular מנחות share with the חביתין but not with the תודה loaves, and says this list is longer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 counted six features that tie regular מנחות to the תודה. Now the גמרא counts eight features that tie them to the חביתין: עשרון, כלי, הקדש, לבונה, מצה, עצם, הגשה and אישים. Using the same 'count the features' rule from step 15, the חביתין should win.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the opposite is true
One tenth of an איפה of flour, the standard amount for a מנחה
Frankincense, put on most מנחות
Bringing the מנחה near the corner of the altar
The fires of the altar
They are more numerous

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two lists. Step 17 counted six features shared with the תודה. This step counts a different set of eight features, shared with the חביתין, and claims this list is the longer one.

phrases.english: On the contrary, from the High Priest's griddle-cakes
phrases.notes: 'He' here is רבי יהודה, whose view of ten loaves the גמרא has been explaining.

phrases.english: he should have learned,
since they share: a tenth, a vessel, consecrated status, and frankincense;
unleavened bread, and coming on its own,
bringing near the altar, and the altar fires,
and these are more numerous.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה, מֵחֲבִיתֵּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses step 17 by showing that the חביתין share more features with regular מנחות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 17 that לחמי תודה are the better model than חביתי כהן גדול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the 'more shared features wins' rule, eight features with the חביתין beat six with the תודה.

steps.title: An ordinary person's offering is learned from an ordinary person's offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה prefers to learn regular מנחות from the תודה, because both are brought by ordinary people. The חביתין are brought by the כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: He prefers to learn an ordinary person's offering from an ordinary person's offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 18. It sets aside counting features and gives a stronger reason to compare with the תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular מנחות and the תודה are both brought by a regular person. The חביתין are a special offering of the כהן גדול. This one deep similarity, who brings the offering, matters more than the number of smaller shared features.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person, as opposed to the כהן גדול
It is preferable to him

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a single basic similarity can outweigh a longer list of technical similarities when choosing a model to learn from.

phrases.english: Learning an ordinary person's offering from an ordinary person's offering is preferable to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a deciding factor that outweighs the feature count.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The model with more shared features, the חביתין, should be used.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shared quality of being an ordinary person's offering makes the תודה the preferred model.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה learns regular מנחות from לחמי תודה (ten loaves), because both are offerings of a הדיוט, even though the חביתין share more features.

steps.title: What is רבי מאיר's reasoning for twelve?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי מאיר from the משנה, who says all מנחות come as twelve loaves, and asks what his reasoning is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: They all come as twelve. What does he hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new opinion in the משנה, רבי מאיר's. It asks for his reasoning and sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's ten loaves came from the תודה. רבי מאיר's twelve must come from a model that has twelve, such as the חביתין or לחם הפנים. The גמרא wants to know which model he uses and why.

keyTerms.meaning: They all come as twelve loaves
What does he hold? What is his reasoning?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּן בָּאוֹת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: They all come as twelve loaves.
What does he hold?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כּוּלָּן בָּאוֹת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה. מַאי קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהודה's view to רבי מאיר's view in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning and source behind רבי מאיר's rule of twelve loaves.

steps.title: First possibility: learn from the חביתין through a בנין אב
steps.stepSummary: Suppose רבי מאיר holds that something learned through a גזירה שוה can go on to teach through a בנין אב. Then he learns from the חביתין, because they share more features.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he holds that a matter learned through a גזירה שוה can then go on and teach through a בנין אב, he learns from חביתי כהן גדול, because these features are more numerous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering its question with a conditional: 'if רבי מאיר holds this rule, then this is his source.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The twelve loaves of the חביתין are themselves something learned through a גזירה שוה. Normally one might ask whether a law learned that way can be used again as a model for a בנין אב. If רבי מאיר says yes, he can use the eight shared features from step 18 and learn twelve from the חביתין.

keyTerms.meaning: A derivation from the same word appearing in two places in the תורה
Using one case as a model to teach a rule for similar cases
Something that was learned then turns around and teaches something else

steps.confusionAlert: This is only an 'if' (אִי). The גמרא is testing one possible reasoning for רבי מאיר, not giving its final answer yet.

phrases.english: If he holds
that a matter learned through a verbal analogy
can then go on and teach as a paradigm,
he learns from the High Priest's griddle-cakes,
phrases.notes: Some versions say דכהן, in round brackets, and the corrected wording is כֹהֵן, in square brackets. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: since these features are more numerous.
phrases.notes: This refers to the eight shared features listed in step 18.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ דְּדָבָר הַלָּמֵד בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּבִנְיַן אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first possible answer to the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If רבי מאיר allows a law learned through a גזירה שוה to teach through a בנין אב, he learns twelve loaves from the חביתין, which share more features with regular מנחות.

steps.title: If he holds the other way, he learns from לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: Suppose רבי מאיר holds that something learned through a גזירה שוה cannot go on to teach through a בנין אב. Then he learns the twelve loaves from לחם הפנים, because both are קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he holds that a matter learned through a גזירה שוה does not turn around and teach through a בנין אב, then he learns from לחם הפנים. He prefers to learn holy offerings from holy offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to explain רבי מאיר's source for twelve loaves. This one works if he holds the opposite rule about learning methods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חביתין got their number through a גזירה שוה, so under this rule they cannot be the model for a בנין אב. So רבי מאיר turns to לחם הפנים, which also has twelve loaves. He chooses it over לחמי תודה because מנחות and לחם הפנים are both at the highest level of holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule that was itself learned through a word-comparison between two פסוקים
Turns around and teaches something further
The twelve showbread loaves placed on the שולחן in the משכן
Learning holy offerings from offerings of the same holy level

steps.whatToRemember: Either way, רבי מאיר reaches twelve loaves. One path learns from the חביתין and the other from לחם הפנים. Which one he uses depends on whether a גזירה שוה result can teach through a בנין אב.

phrases.english: If he holds
that a matter learned through a verbal analogy
does not turn around and teach through a paradigm
he learns it from the showbread,
learning consecrated from consecrated is better for him.
phrases.notes: Regular מנחות and לחם הפנים are both of the highest holiness. The תודה loaves are a lower level.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ דְּדָבָר הַלָּמֵד בִּגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה אֵינוֹ חוֹזֵר וּמְלַמֵּד בְּבִנְיַן אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the 'if he holds' split begun in step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רבי מאיר's source for twelve loaves?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: If a rule learned through a גזירה שוה cannot teach through a בנין אב, he learns from לחם הפנים, since both are of the same high holiness

steps.title: Quoting the exceptions in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of רבי מאיר in the משנה. לחמי תודה and the loaves of נזירות are exceptions and come in tens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for לחמי תודה and the loaves of נזירות, which come as ten each.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exception to set up its next move. The next steps explain where each exception comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said every מנחה comes as twelve loaves. Here he leaves out two kinds of offerings that come in sets of ten. The גמרא will give a source for each one.

keyTerms.meaning: The loaves brought with a קרבן תודה (thanksgiving offering)
The offerings a נזיר brings when he finishes his נזירות
Ten of each kind

phrases.english: Except for the loaves of the thanks offering and naziriteship,
which come as ten each.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּץ מִלַּחְמֵי תוֹדָה וּנְזִירוּת, שֶׁהֵן בָּאוֹת עֶשֶׂר עֶשֶׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from רבי מאיר's general rule to his stated exceptions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, לחמי תודה and the loaves of נזירות come as ten of each kind, not twelve

steps.title: The source for ten תודה loaves
steps.stepSummary: The number for לחמי תודה is written openly in the תורה's own section about them.
steps.simpleTranslation: לחמי תודה: it is written about them explicitly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first exception. The תודה does not need to learn from anywhere else, because its rule is stated directly about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בנין אב is only needed when a קרבן has no rule of its own. The תודה loaves have their own source, so the general twelve-loaf rule does not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Openly, explicitly

phrases.english: The loaves of the thanks offering:
it is written about them explicitly.
phrases.notes: The תודה's own פסוקים in ויקרא 7 give its rule, so there is nothing to borrow from other offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first exception quoted in step 23
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do the לחמי תודה come in tens?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their rule is stated directly in their own פסוקים

steps.title: The source for ten loaves of the נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The word "שלמיו" in the תודה section includes the שלמי נזיר, so the נזיר's loaves follow the תודה's ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: נזירות: as the Master said, "שלמיו" (his peace offerings) comes to include the שלמי נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second exception. A word in the תודה's פסוק pulls the נזיר's loaves into the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא quotes a teaching that the word "שלמיו" (his peace offerings) in the תודה section comes to include the נזיר's שלמים. Since the נזיר's offering is included in the תודה's rule, his loaves also come as ten each.

keyTerms.meaning: "His peace offerings" (ויקרא 7:13)
To include something extra
The peace offering a נזיר brings at the end of his נזירות

steps.whatToRemember: Both exceptions have their own source. The תודה is stated directly, and the נזיר is included through the word "שלמיו". That is why they come as ten and not twelve.

phrases.english: Naziriteship:
as the Master said:
"His peace offerings"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:13

phrases.english: comes to include the peace offering of the nazirite.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְזִירוּת – דְּאָמַר מָר: ״שְׁלָמָיו״ – לְרַבּוֹת שַׁלְמֵי נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second exception from step 23 by linking it to the תודה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why do the loaves of נזירות come in tens?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "שלמיו" includes the שלמי נזיר in the תודה's rule

steps.title: שמואל: four big תודה loaves still work
steps.stepSummary: רב טובי בר קיסנא quotes שמואל: if someone baked the תודה loaves as only four loaves, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טובי בר קיסנא said that שמואל said: לחמי תודה that he baked as four loaves, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from שמואל. If someone made just four big תודה loaves instead of the usual set, the offering still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תודה has four kinds of bread. The usual way is to bring ten of each kind. שמואל says that one loaf of each kind, four in total, is still good after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: He baked them
He has fulfilled his obligation

phrases.english: Rav Tovi bar Kisna said,
Shmuel said:
Loaves of the thanks offering that he baked as four loaves,
he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב טוֹבִי בַּר קִיסְנָא, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how many תודה loaves are truly required
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four תודה loaves, one of each kind, are good after the fact

steps.title: But we need forty loaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: the תודה needs forty loaves, ten of each kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we require forty?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל's ruling. How can four be enough when the rule is forty?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, the גמרא said the תודה loaves come as ten of each kind. Four kinds times ten makes forty. Four loaves seems to clash with that number.

keyTerms.meaning: But don't we require
Forty loaves, ten of each of the four kinds

phrases.english: But we require forty?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling in step 26
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that four loaves are enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תודה needs ten loaves of each of four kinds, forty in all, so four should not be enough

steps.title: Forty is only the best way
steps.stepSummary: Forty loaves is the ideal way to do the מצוה, but four still counts after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in one word. Forty is needed only to do the מצוה in the best way, not to make the offering valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא separates the best way to do something (למצוה) from what is needed for it to count (יצא). Forty is the ideal, and four is enough for him to fulfill his obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: For doing the מצוה in the best way, but not required for it to count

steps.whatToRemember: For the תודה, forty loaves is the ideal, but four loaves, one of each kind, still works after the fact.
steps.confusionAlert: "Required for the מצוה" does not mean "required for it to count." Here, forty is only the ideal.

phrases.english: For the מצוה!
phrases.notes: Forty is how it should be done at the start. If he brought only four, it still counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating the best way to do the מצוה from what is needed for it to count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forty loaves is required for the תודה to count at all
steps.terutzMaskana: Forty is the ideal, but four loaves are enough after the fact

steps.title: How can תרומה be taken from only four loaves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל: the owner has to separate תרומה from the תודה loaves, so how can that work if there are only four?
steps.simpleTranslation: But he has to separate תרומה from them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on שמואל again. The owner must give one loaf of each kind to the כהן as תרומה, and with only four loaves that seems impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 28 said four loaves still count after the fact. Now the גמרא points to another part of the מצוה: setting aside תרומה for the כהן. If there is only one loaf of each kind, taking one of each as תרומה does not seem workable.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of the תודה loaves (one of each kind) that is given to the כהן
To separate, to set aside

phrases.english: But he needs to separate
phrases.notes: "He" is the person bringing the תודה.

phrases.english: תרומה from them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to שמואל after the answer in step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that four loaves are enough after the fact
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומה requires one loaf of each kind for the כהן, which seems impossible when only one loaf of each kind exists

steps.title: Cutting a piece from each loaf does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests he could cut a piece from each loaf as תרומה, then rejects this because the פסוק says 'one', meaning a whole loaf, not a slice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he separates a piece from each and every loaf, the תורה says 'one', which teaches that he may not take a sliced piece.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a possible way out and shuts it down right away. You cannot cut a slice from each loaf, because the תרומה must be a whole loaf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea was to give the כהן a portion of each of the four loaves instead of a whole loaf. The פסוק's word 'אחד' (one) teaches that the תרומה must be one complete loaf, so a cut piece is not allowed. This makes the challenge from step 29 stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a possible answer that the גמרא is about to reject
A sliced or broken piece of bread
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה

phrases.english: And if you would say that he separates
from each and every one –
phrases.notes: He means cutting a portion off each loaf instead of giving a whole loaf.

phrases.english: the Merciful One said "one,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:14

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּמַפְרֵישׁ מִכֹּל חֲדָא וַחֲדָא

steps.title: He set the תרומה aside while kneading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that he separated the תרומה portions at the kneading stage, before baking, so it does not count as taking a sliced piece.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he separated them while kneading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The portions were set aside while the dough was still being kneaded, not cut from finished loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem of 'פרוס' only applies when you cut into a baked loaf. If the תרומה portions were set aside from the dough while kneading, nothing was ever sliced off a loaf. So שמואל's ruling of four loaves can still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: Kneading, the stage of making the dough before baking

phrases.english: Where he separated them during kneading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 29 and 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific way of doing it (separating at the kneading stage)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only four loaves, the תרומה would have to be a slice cut from a loaf, which the פסוק forbids
steps.terutzMaskana: The portions were set aside from the dough during kneading, so no loaf was sliced

steps.title: A ברייתא says the number of תודה loaves cannot change
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from a ברייתא: most מנחות are still valid with more or fewer loaves, but the תודה loaves are listed as an exception.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: All מנחות where one added to or reduced the number of loaves are valid, except for the לחם הפנים, the חביתי כהן גדול, and the loaves of the תודה and of נזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to directly contradict שמואל. It lists the תודה loaves among the offerings whose number cannot be changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said four תודה loaves work after the fact. The ברייתא says that changing the number of loaves makes the תודה invalid. So it seems the full forty loaves are required, even after the fact.
